```{python}
# Authenticating my API
kaggle.api.authenticate()
kaggle.api.dataset_download_files('hummaamqaasim/jobs-in-data', path='.', unzip=True)

# download the csv dataset into dataframe
df = pd.read_csv('cleansing_exploration_datasets/jobs_in_data.csv')

# check for missing values
df.isna().sum()

# check datatypes of each column
df.dtypes

# filter dataset for only US based companies and employees that have a residence in the US
df = df[(df['employee_residence'].isin(['United States'])) & df['company_location'].isin(['United States'])]

# see what years this dataset covers
df['job_category'].unique()
```

```{python}
# Filtering the dataset to only include the year 2023
df1 = df.loc[(df['work_year'] == 2023)].reset_index(drop=True)
# I group by job category and the mean salary in USD
df1 = round(df1.groupby('job_category').agg(
      avg_salary=('salary_in_usd', 'mean'),
      job_count=('job_category', 'count')
    ).reset_index(),2)

# Here I create my line graph to see salaries for each job title in the US
(
  ggplot(df1, aes(x = 'avg_salary', y = 'job_category', fill='job_category'))
  # Here I create line and give it a size
  + geom_bar(size = 1.5, stat='identity', show_legend= False)
  # Here I have the different colors for each line
  + scale_color_manual(values=['#66FF03','#ff000d','#ffff00', '#0099ff', '#f58231',
                                '#911eb4', '#fabed4', '#f032e6', '#dcbeff', '#800000'])
  # Here I change the scale intervals in the x-axis and y-axis and format the x-axis years to not show a comma
  + scale_x_continuous(format= ',d', breaks=np.arange(0, 250000, step=50000))
  # + scale_y_continuous(breaks=np.arange(95000, 200000, step=50000))
  # Here I cut off any part of the graph I do not need
  # + coord_cartesian(xlim=(1920, 2000), ylim=(0, 55000))
  + theme(
        # change the complete background to black
        plot_background=element_rect(fill='#36454F'),
        # changing the grid color lines to shade of white. Also changed size of the grid lines
        panel_grid=element_line(color='#E2DFD2', size=1),
        # this is how I changed the y-axis and x-axis numbers labels to white, as well as their respective titles
        axis_text = element_text(color='white'),
        # axis_title = element_text(color='white'),
        # this is how I made the title and subtitle white
        title = element_text(color='white'),
        # Here I make the y-axis labels smaller
        axis_text_y=element_text(size=9),
        # Here I make the x-axis labels smaller
        axis_text_x=element_text(size=10),
        # Here I change the position of the title and subtitle to be on the left side of the plot
        plot_title_position='plot',
        # Here I add a margin around the entire plot
        plot_margin = 25,
        axis_title=element_text(size=13)
      )
  # Here I add the title, subtitle, x-axis and y-axis titles
  + labs(
        title = 'Salaries for Each Job Title in the US',
        subtitle = '2023 Results',
        x = 'Average Salary in USD',
        y = 'Job Category' 
        )
)
```

```{python}
        x = '',
        y = 'Job Count',
        fill='Job Category'

)
```

```{python}
# source - Texas one year estimate jobs by specialization
# https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT1Y2023.B15012?q=texas+education+degrees+in+2023


data = requests.get('https://api.census.gov/data/2023/acs/acs1?get=group(B15012)&ucgid=0400000US48').json()

variables= ['B15012_002E','B15012_003E','B15012_004E','B15012_005E','B15012_006E','B15012_007E','B15012_008E','B15012_009E', 'B15012_010E','B15012_011E','B15012_012E','B15012_013E','B15012_014E','B15012_015E','B15012_016E']

labels= ['Computers, Mathematics, and Statistics','Bilogical, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences','Physical and Related Sciences','Psychology',
         'Social Sciences','Engineering','Multidisciplinary Studies','Science and Engineering Related Fields','Business','Education',
         'Literature and Languages','Liberal Arts and History','Visual and Performing Arts','Communications','Other']

# B15012_002E: Science and Engineering- Computers, Mathematics, and Statistics
# B15012_003E: Science and Engineering- Bilogical, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences
# B15012_004E: Science and Engineering- Physical and Related Sciences
# B15012_005E: Science and Engineering- Psychology
# B15012_006E: Science and Engineering- Social Sciences
# B15012_007E: Science and Engineering- Engineering
# B15012_008E: Science and Engineering- Multidisciplinary Studies
# B15012_009E: Science and Engineering- Science and Engineering Related Fields
# B15012_010E: Science and Engineering- Business
# B15012_011E: Science and Engineering- Education
# B15012_012E: Arts, Humanities, and Other- Literature and Languages
# B15012_013E: Arts, Humanities, and Other- Liberal Arts and History
# B15012_014E: Arts, Humanities, and Other- Visual and Performing Arts
# B15012_015E: Arts, Humanities, and Other- Communications
# B15012_016E: Arts, Humanities, and Other- Other

# Created a dataframe with the data from the API
df2 = pd.DataFrame(data)
# Changed column names
df2.columns= df2.iloc[0]
# Dropped the first row of the dataframe
df2 = df2.drop(df2.index[0])

# filtered the dataframe to only include the columns I need
df2 = df2[['B15012_002E','B15012_003E','B15012_004E','B15012_005E','B15012_006E','B15012_007E','B15012_008E','B15012_009E', 'B15012_010E','B15012_011E','B15012_012E','B15012_013E','B15012_014E','B15012_015E','B15012_016E']]

for index, value in enumerate(df2.columns):
  df2 = df2.rename(columns={df2.columns[index]: labels[index]})

df2.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)
df2 = df2.melt()

df2 = df2.rename(columns={0: 'Specialization', 'value':'Total Estimated'}).sort_values(by='Total Estimated', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

df2
```

```{python}
# Employment data for Texas
# https://data.bls.gov/oes/#/area/4800000

#Selenium link
# https://builtin.com/articles/selenium-web-scraping

cService = webdriver.ChromeService(executable_path='C:/Users/lrive/Downloads/chromedriver-win64/chromedriver-win64/chromedriver.exe')
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=cService)

driver.get('https://data.bls.gov/oes/#/area/4800000')

# Wait for the table body to be present (I adjust the time in seconds as needed)
WebDriverWait(driver, 20).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located((By.XPATH, '//*[@id="oes-container"]/div/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/table/tbody/tr[1]'))
)

table_body = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, '//*[@id="oes-container"]/div/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/table/tbody')
table_rows = table_body.find_elements(By.TAG_NAME, 'tr')

headers_list = []
rows_list = []
for item in driver.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//*[@id="oes-container"]/div/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/table/tbody/tr'):
  if item.text != '':
    # first I split the text with comma as the delimiter wherever a new line occurs (this happens once every row)
    row = item.text.split('\n')
    # Here I append the first string value in the row to the list
    rows_list.append(row[0])
    # Here I replace any dash in the second string with a space
    row[1] = row[1].translate(str.maketrans({'-': ' '}))
    # Here I split the second string with a comma wherever a space occurs - these strings are in their own list (list within a list)
    row[1] = row[1].split(' ')
    # I append the items in the nested list to the rows_list variable
    for value in row[1]:
      rows_list.append(value)
    # if len(item.text) > 0:
      # rows_list.append(item.text)
      # rows_list.append(individual_item)
# driver.quit()

# I now use list comprehension to remove any empty strings in the list
new_rows_list = [non_blank_value for non_blank_value in rows_list if non_blank_value != '']

for item in driver.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//*[@id="oes-container"]/div/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/table/thead/tr/th'):
  if item.text != '':
    headers_list.append(item.text)
    
driver.quit()

```
